I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I have well irrigation, long farming experience, and a relatively educated household, so I will run a fairly input-stable plan rather than a low-input gamble. Wheat and maize are still my backbone because they fit my land, my machinery rhythm, and local conditions in Quzhou County. I will put `10.0 mu` into the wheat-maize rotation and `3.1 mu` into cotton. That gives me grain security, cash income diversification, and a workload my family can still manage even though some members work off-farm.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, fertilize steadily, and irrigate twice. At the start of the season, I care most about a uniform stand and strong early growth, because that sets up the whole wheat side of the year. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient on my scale and fits the wheat-maize system well. I will keep pesticide use moderate and only plan for two applications, because I want to control disease and aphids without overspending. My yield target is solid rather than extreme.

For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep the same `10.0 mu` after wheat. I will lean toward no-tillage after wheat harvest because it saves time, preserves moisture, and helps me turn the land around fast. I will push nitrogen a little higher than wheat because maize responds well when water is available, and I do have well irrigation. I will plan two irrigations and two pesticide applications. My main objective is stable grain filling and avoiding yield loss from delayed field operations.

For cotton, I will keep it on the smaller block because it takes more management and more pest attention. I will use hybrid seed, keep potassium a bit stronger than in grain crops, and irrigate three times because cotton needs steady moisture through squaring and boll setting. I will plan more pesticide applications than wheat or maize because cotton insect pressure is usually the most demanding part of the farm. I will use rotary tillage there too, because it gives me a clean seedbed and a manageable start. I am not trying to maximize cotton area; I am keeping it as a controlled cash crop alongside my main grain rotation.
